territorial_scope.description: Reaches covered entities headquartered in, organized under the laws of, or subject to the jurisdiction of countries of concern, including foreign entities, and applies to federal procurement and CFIUS review.

evidence.quote: an entity with its headquarters located in, organized under the laws of, or otherwise subject to the jurisdiction of, a country of concern

summary.short: Bill would bar federal executive agencies and their contractors from buying or using humanoid robots made by covered entities tied to countries of concern, subject covered-nation investments in US humanoid-robot businesses to CFIUS review and mandatory declarations, and require a Defense Department threat report. Procurement bans apply 180 days after enactment.
summary.long: As introduced, the bill covers humanoid robots made by covered entities, including governments and political parties of countries of concern, certain foreign entities, Chinese military companies listed under NDAA section 1260H, and entities headquartered in or subject to such countries' jurisdiction. Section 3 bars executive agencies from procuring such robots and bars contractors from using them to perform awarded contracts, with a Secretary of Defense waiver for national security or research; the bans apply 180 days after enactment, and the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council must amend the FAR within 180 days, including prime-contractor flow-down. Section 4 amends the Defense Production Act's CFIUS provisions to cover, subject to regulations, covered-nation investments in US businesses that design, test, develop or manufacture humanoid robots, and requires declarations for such covered transactions; these amendments apply to transactions proposed or pending on or after enactment. Section 5 requires the Secretary of Defense, within one year, to report to specified committees on national security threats from humanoid robots in countries of concern, including export controls, intellectual property, data privacy and security, with recommendations. The text sets no penalties.

notes: No legal_basis or enacted_by_bill relation is stated in the text. Sec. 4 amends the Defense Production Act through strike-and-insert instructions that do not reproduce the resulting statutory text. Sec. 4(b) requires declarations 'described in subclause (I)' without restating that subclause; the reference is read as the existing text of section 721(b)(1)(C)(v)(IV)(bb). Sec. 2(2) and Sec. 4(a)(2)(vi)(II)(aa) both use the 'covered nation' term from 10 U.S.C. 4872. Text is the bill as introduced.

thresholds.note: The bill contains no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Its only numbers are procedural time limits: 180 days for the effective date in Sec. 3(d) and for the FAR amendment in Sec. 3(e), and one year for the report in Sec. 5(a). These are coded as deadline events, not thresholds. The definitions in Sec. 2 and the amended Defense Production Act text in Sec. 4 contain no numeric cutoffs, and the Sec. 3(c) waiver is not numeric.
